scope: Source-bound explanation of the Batch 01 r4 implementation. Original r1 design attachments are proposals. These descriptions establish executable mechanism, not performance or isolated LLM benefit.

source_verification.method: Read-only byte comparison of the six listed Runtime 004 modules with entries inside the frozen r4 ZIP; every comparison matched.
source_verification.administration: Later r4-admin-001 revisions preserve the original physical/policy/model configuration and add separately adopted execution administration. They do not add new architecture mechanisms.

model.name: Qwen3-14B Q4_K_M
model.runtime: Local llama.cpp b9000; thinking disabled; temperature 0; one outstanding request per candidate
model.overflow: Reject before generation; no silent truncation or automatic summarization
model.placement: A local gateway outside the isolated candidate process runs the model. Sensing and execution workers are conventional infrastructure, not additional LLM agents.

input.candidate_packet: Current versioned order, image-derived tagged-object detections with ages, public station state, inspection response, gripper state, joint telemetry, bounded command feedback and public process contract.
input.llm_context: Two-message request: fixed system instructions plus JSON containing current order, fresh visible detections, station/gripper state, fixture belief, public process contract, auxiliary detections, retained part records, computed progress, errors/failure counts, up to eight recent resolutions and public human answers. A1/A2 also receive an unranked admissible-action menu; A3 receives its scheduled transport.
input.distinction: The policy process can receive joint telemetry and inspection responses, but _context does not copy every packet field into the model prompt. Inspection evidence is represented through retained part records. Raw camera images are not fed to this text model.
input.permissions: No hidden poses, evaluator truth, protected seeds, future disturbances, operator map, repository history or previous evaluation results are candidate memory.

steps: Ingest observed evidence and reconcile pending action
Choose or interpret a task decision
Validate against current public conditions and order
Gateway admission and bounded shared execution
control_loop.physics: MuJoCo advances at a 0.002 s simulation step. The workcell and machine timers keep advancing during inference, geometry planning and candidate restart.
control_loop.decision_timing: Approximately 10 Hz decision opportunities, delayed while a model request or a macro action is active. There is no model invocation per servo tick.
control_loop.motion: Transport uses a fixed Cartesian waypoint sequence: lift/approach, descend, close jaws, lift, transit, lower, release, retreat and return to the clear-view posture. IK produces joint targets; smooth quintic interpolation drives the shared actuator controls. Object movement follows contact dynamics.
control_loop.completion: A trajectory ending is command status. The candidate requires public evidence to resolve placement/process/inspection. The separate protected evaluator determines physical success and final task completion.
control_loop.dispatch_branches: Motion operations use shared planners and actuators; cycle and inspect use public device services. Ordinary observe/wait return status, clear-view observe invokes arm retreat, help uses the public assistance service, and done triggers a protected completion check.

shared.operation_meaning: Transport moves a visible part; cycle processes an already loaded eligible part; inspect measures a part already on the inspection pad; setup physically exchanges the fixture insert. Movement does not perform processing or inspection implicitly.

read_write_flow: Worker constructs Candidate(kind, Path('/work'), persistent). Candidate loads candidate-state.json if present and validates checksum, version and kind.
Each public packet updates Python state; reconciliation distinguishes intent, feedback and fresh observed outcome.
The runtime serializes a changed state to a temporary file, flushes/fsyncs it, atomically replaces candidate-state.json and emits a context_write evidence event.
Before a model request, host policy code assembles selected state fields into JSON. The model receives that JSON; it has no file-read, file-write, shell or general tool loop.
Model JSON is parsed and validated by policy code. A1/A3 queue a proposal in process memory; A2 commits its program into checkpoint state.
Before action dispatch, the runtime checkpoints the intent and pending action. Feedback plus fresh public observations later update the checkpoint.

Restart creates a new worker and incarnation. Persistent /work reloads the checkpoint. No-persistence /work is newly created; the supervisor also resets its assigned candidate_state directory. Current public order/device observations remain available.

limitations: This is a simplified simulated Panda workcell, with colored tags and fixed services; it is not real-robot or unrestricted visual manipulation evidence.
A full-system comparison changes where the LLM acts and how often it is called. It does not isolate language reasoning from scheduling, prompts or runtime behavior.
Source inspection demonstrates what code does. Performance, recovery qualification and causal persistence benefit require the corresponding valid run evidence.
Recorded context bytes, bytes supplied to a gateway, successful model ingestion and meaningful model use are different claims.
No-persistence removes private history at runtime restart, not every decision; it is not a policy with no within-incarnation memory.

architectures.name: Durable Conventional Sequencer
architectures.mechanism: Explicit public-evidence rules select every job operation; the common planner and actuator stack carry it out. No LLM is called.
architectures.decision: Repair amended tray placements, inspect or route staged parts, finish/unload fixture work, then select matching raw stock; wait or request help when public evidence does not support progress.

architectures.name: Durable Task Dispatcher
architectures.mechanism: For normal task decisions, the LLM chooses one typed action from the shared unranked menu of currently admissible public actions.
architectures.llm_input: Common JSON context plus currently_admissible_actions. The menu contains legal alternatives and multiple stock IDs; it does not expose the conventional scheduler's preferred next step.
architectures.llm_output: One JSON action object. It is parsed, queued, checked against the current order and public preconditions, checkpointed and dispatched.

architectures.name: Guarded Procedure Composer
architectures.role: LLM authors a short guarded action list
architectures.mechanism: The LLM emits 1–8 action nodes with up to five guards each. On a decision, a deterministic interpreter scans incomplete nodes in order and executes the first whose guards are true and whose action is currently eligible.
architectures.llm_input: Common JSON context plus the public admissible-action menu and allowed guard/action schema.
architectures.llm_output: A steps array of guards and actions. The runtime validates it and checkpoints a program ID, order version, steps, completed-node list and source context sequence.

architectures.name: Grounded Objective Composer
architectures.mechanism: The conventional sequencer selects every job operation. For a selected transport, the LLM supplies clearance, speed scale, vertical approach and named avoidance zones. Other operations proceed without an A3 model call.
architectures.llm_input: Common JSON context plus the conventional scheduler's scheduled_action.
architectures.llm_output: clearance 0.08–0.25 m, speed_scale 0.3–1.0, approach='vertical', avoid_zones. Source and destination zones cannot be forbidden.

architectures.design_difference: Despite the inherited architecture name, this implementation does not repeatedly optimize a language-defined cost against new observations. It uses a fixed Cartesian waypoint/IK transport template, with bounded model-selected parameters.
limitations: Named-zone checks sample TCP xy positions at 21 points per joint segment, including the return leg; they do not certify whole-arm or payload clearance
The model cannot change stock order, task order, torques or the exact trajectory
A rejected avoidance constraint does not trigger a general obstacle-routing optimizer
